title: Homogeneous and inhomogeneous unit cohomology
statement: For every field K, the continuous homogeneous degree-two cohomology GaloisUnitsH2 K [def-sc-galois-units-cohomology] is in bijection with GaloisUnitsTwoCocycleClasses K [def-sc-galois-units-two-cocycle-classes]. Both use the Krull topology on Gal(Ks/K) and the discrete natural module of separable-closure units. No etale sheaf cohomology occurs in this comparison.

proof.text: The Galois group is compact Hausdorff. Each coefficient is algebraic, hence has open stabilizer in the Krull topology; discreteness makes the action jointly continuous. Apply the compact-open exponential law to identify iterated continuous maps with maps on finite products. The recursive differential expands inductively to the alternating omission differential.

Send an equivariant homogeneous cochain f to c(g1,...,gn)=f(1,g1,g1g2,...,g1...gn). Its inverse is f(g0,...,gn)=g0 • c(g0⁻¹g1,...,g(n-1)⁻¹gn). Equivariance proves they are inverse; group operations and the jointly continuous action prove continuity. Omitting the first, interior and last coordinates gives respectively the action term, adjacent-product terms and final term of the inhomogeneous differential.

In degree two this identifies kernel with the stated continuous two-cocycles, and the preceding differential has formula g • b(h)-b(gh)+b(g). TopModuleCat kernels and cokernels use the underlying algebraic kernel and quotient, so the equivalences descend to mutually inverse maps on the continuous-coboundary quotient.
